questions.stem: Minutes after an IV antibiotic begins, a client develops generalized hives, wheezing, facial swelling, and hypotension. Which medication should the nurse prepare to give first for the suspected anaphylaxis?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"IV diphenhydramine because antihistamine therapy reverses the airway and circulatory manifestations of anaphylaxis more rapidly than epinephrine.","B":"IV methylprednisolone because corticosteroids provide the fastest treatment for acute hypotension and bronchospasm during anaphylaxis.","C":"Intramuscular epinephrine in the mid-outer thigh while emergency support, airway assessment, and additional resuscitation measures are initiated.","D":"Nebulized albuterol alone because bronchodilation treats the life-threatening component of anaphylaxis even when hypotension is also present."}}
questions.rationale: Current anaphylaxis guidance continues to identify prompt intramuscular epinephrine in the mid-outer thigh as first-line treatment. Antihistamines, corticosteroids, and inhaled bronchodilators may have adjunctive roles but do not replace epinephrine for a systemic reaction with airway/breathing and circulatory compromise.
questions.source_detail: Current guidance identifies prompt intramuscular epinephrine in the mid-outer thigh as the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis.

questions.stem: A client who recently stopped long-term prednisone presents with persistent vomiting, profound weakness, and blood pressure of 78/42 mm Hg. Glucocorticoid-induced adrenal insufficiency has not been ruled out. What should the nurse anticipate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Oral prednisone after the vomiting resolves because parenteral therapy is unnecessary unless laboratory testing first confirms adrenal insufficiency.","B":"Immediate parenteral glucocorticoid treatment and fluid resuscitation while the client is promptly evaluated for adrenal crisis and precipitating factors.","C":"Fluid restriction and observation because hypotension after stopping glucocorticoids is expected and usually resolves without hormone replacement.","D":"Delay glucocorticoid therapy until a morning cortisol result returns because treating before biochemical confirmation would make the diagnosis unreliable now."}}
questions.rationale: The 2024 Endocrine Society/European Society of Endocrinology guideline states that adrenal crisis should be considered in patients with current or recent glucocorticoid use who develop hemodynamic instability, vomiting, or diarrhea when recovery has not been demonstrated. Suspected crisis should be treated promptly with parenteral glucocorticoids and fluid resuscitation rather than waiting for confirmatory testing.
questions.source_name: Endocrine Society / European Society of Endocrinology — Glucocorticoid-Induced Adrenal Insufficiency Guideline
questions.source_detail: 2024 recommendation: consider adrenal crisis with hemodynamic instability or persistent vomiting/diarrhea after glucocorticoid exposure and treat with parenteral glucocorticoids plus fluids.
